marble.name: Joining Letters
marble.subject: English
marble.description: Begin to join letters using diagonal and horizontal strokes, understanding which letter pairs are best left unjoined, forming letters of correct size relative to one another
marble.prompt: Is you starting to join up their letters when writing, so that their handwriting flows more smoothly rather than each letter standing completely separate?

cluster.summary: Your child is mastering the physical skills of writing — learning to form letters and numbers correctly, hold a pencil properly, and develop neat, legible handwriting.

representations: Lined paper with ascender and descender guides
Unjoined-letter list for the school scheme
authoredAnswer: Joins follow the scheme: diagonal joins from the baseline where the letter finishes there (m-u, u-c, c-h in much; k-i, i-n, n-d in kind), horizontal joins from letters finishing at the top (o-w, w-n in town), and letters the scheme leaves unjoined after them (for example b and y in boys) left unjoined. Letters keep correct relative size, ascenders and descenders do not clash, and downstrokes are roughly parallel.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Drops horizontal joins to the baseline, distorting letters such as o, w and v and the letter after them. Evidence basis: Education Endowment Foundation, Improving Literacy in Key Stage 1 (second edition), Box 6 (National
wrongAnswers.fix: Practise the horizontal join set alone in short rows with a top-line guide; then return to words containing o and w.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Letter size, shape or spacing deteriorates when joining is attempted. Evidence basis: Education Endowment Foundation, Improving Literacy in Key Stage 1 (second edition), Box 6 (National Handwriting Association) on joinin
wrongAnswers.fix: Return to secure unjoined letters of correct size for a period, as the National Handwriting Association advice in the EEF report suggests, before reintroducing one join set at a time.
